requirement:
For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.

For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
rationale:
The tests adequately cover every obligation of `requirements.authoring.cache_checkpoints`.

**Backends.** Bedrock is the only backend that takes explicit checkpoints. `RigProvider::connect` sets `caches` from `bedrock_caches` for Bedrock and to false for OpenAI and Ollama. `complete` calls `place_cache_checkpoints` only when `caches` is true.

**Bedrock, supporting model: a checkpoint after the system prompt and one at the end of the last message, on every request.**
- `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[claude_requests_carry_cache_checkpoints_and_record_cache_usage]` runs a two-request Claude conversation.
- For each request body it asserts two things. The `system` array has exactly two entries: the "# Task" text, then the `cachePoint` block. The last content block of the last message is a `cachePoint`.
- It asserts that `cachePoint` appears exactly twice in each body, so there are no extra checkpoints.
- The second request follows a reasoning turn and a tool result. It also ends in a checkpoint, so "every request" covers later requests as well as the first.
- The first request ends the subject message, and the second ends the tool-result message.

**Backend or model without caching support.**
- The "when the backend and model support prompt caching" condition is tested in two places.
- In the CLI test, `fixture-uncached-model` produces a request with no `cachePoint`.
- In `providers.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cache_checkpoints_are_requested_for_caching_models]`, `bedrock_caches` accepts the Claude and Nova model IDs and rejects Llama and the fixture model.

**Checkpoints MUST NOT change content.**
- The CLI test compares each cached request with the uncached-model request after `without_cache_points` removes only the `cachePoint` blocks. The two bodies must be equal.
- The unit test shows that `place_cache_checkpoints` changes only `options.cache`. It does this by comparing the JSON of the request with an expected request that has only the cache option set. It also covers a request that has a reasoning turn.

**OpenAI.** `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[openai_responses_replays_tool_calls_and_records_usage]` checks the following.
- The `instructions` and `tools` are identical across the two requests.
- The second request's `input` starts with exactly the first request's `input`, in order. It then adds the `function_call` and `function_call_output` items.
- The recursive `assert_no_checkpoints` helper rejects `cachePoint`, `cache_control`, and `cache_point` or `cache_checkpoint` block types anywhere in either request body. This covers the "MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks" obligation.

**Out of scope.** The same system prompt for every assessment of a kind belongs to `requirements.authoring.prompt_parts`, which is cited here and tested separately.

I found no gaps.

For backends that accept explicit cache checkpoints, when the backend and model
support prompt caching, every provider request MUST place one cache checkpoint
after the system prompt of {cite}`requirements.authoring.prompt_parts` and
another at the end of its last message, so each request reuses the tool
definitions and system prompt that earlier assessments of its kind sent, and
the conversation its own earlier requests sent. Cache checkpoints MUST NOT
change the content of a request.
For OpenAI, which caches matching prompt prefixes automatically, the harness
MUST keep the system prompt and tool definitions unchanged across requests in
one conversation and replay prior conversation content in its original order.
It MUST NOT insert checkpoint blocks.
:::{req} prompt_parts
Each assessment conversation MUST send its prompt as a system prompt followed by
one user message, the subject message, filled from the first and second text
blocks of the prompt requirement for the assessment's kind. The kinds are
test-adequacy requirement, structural requirement, example, citation review, site
review, and a verifier of each of those. A system prompt MUST be the same for
every assessment of its kind, so every placeholder whose value depends on the
subject MUST be in the subject message.
